# thermodynamic_solver — wiring list (generated by gen_bbrd_thermo.py)

A **fresh full-size breadboard**, not the 1b board. **This board is powered.**

Each node is driven by its own **resistor Johnson-noise source** (R11/R12, 10k) into a
two-stage zero-drift front end: **stage 1 x11, stage 2 x101, total x1111 nominal**
(1125 and 1130 from the measured gain-set resistors). Johnson noise is white from DC to
~THz by the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, which is exactly what `Sigma = c G^-1`
requires.

> **NEVER RAISE STAGE-1 GAIN.** Taking stage 1 from x11 to x101 (R7/R8 -> 100k) makes an
> 80 dB chain and oscillates at 89.6 kHz on this breadboard; x11 is stable. For more
> level change R13/R14 (stage 2, fed from a low-impedance output) -- never R7/R8.

**Power (bench PSU SPD3303X-E, series-tracked to +/-12 V):**
- `top_plus` + `bot_plus` rails = **+12 V (PWR_P)**, joined across banks.
- `top_minus` + `bot_minus` rails = **POWER GROUND ONLY**, joined across banks. They
  carry the op-amp supply return (~5 mA) and nothing else. The left/right jumper at
  cols 30<->34 is for the KiCad model; this board joins the halves internally.

**GROUND ARCHITECTURE (2026-09-07) — read this before wiring.** The signal grounds are
a star system that is kept OFF the power rails:

```
  C1, C2, R4 returns --> NETWORK SUB-STAR (col 25, top bank)
                                  |
  ch A star (col 50) -----------> MAIN STAR (col 52, bottom) --[i52, ONE wire]--> rails
  ch B star (col 53) -----------/
```

The op-amps' ~5 mA supply return runs decoupling caps -> rails -> PSU lead. Previously
the network grounded onto those same rails at cols 24/26/36, putting its 0 V reference
*inside* the supply-return path: 5 mA x ~0.1 ohm is ~0.5 mV, which is what we measured
at the nodes (0.45 mV) and why v1 shifted 21% (4.5 sigma) merely by moving a scope clip.
Signal currents are ~0.2 uA and could never have caused it. Now no supply current can
flow through the star system at all, because it reaches the rails through one wire.
**Scope and DMM grounds go on the star (col 52 / col 50), never on a rail.**
- Column 51 (bottom) = **-12 V (PWR_N)** — only the op-amp V- pins need it. NOTE:
  col 53 is ch B's SIGNAL-GROUND STAR — do not confuse the two.
- **Set the PSU current limit to 50 mA per rail** before enabling output. Quiescent
  draw is < 10 mA/rail; 50 mA is a hard cap that protects a wiring slip. Verify each
  rail with the DMM before connecting. **This board still never touches skin.**

Hole names: row letter + column (`c20` = row c, column 20). Holes sharing a column
within a bank are connected by the board; the two banks (rows a-e / f-j) are separate.
The passive RC network is in the top bank (cols 10-40). The front end occupies cols
46-59: per channel, stage 1 in the BOTTOM bank (op-amp pins 1-3) and stage 2 in the
TOP bank (pins 5-7).

**Nodes:** node 1 = column 20. Node 2 = column 30, extended to column 32 by the e30->e32
wire so that both nodes have spare holes for a scope probe and a DMM lead.

**DMM-measure before plugging** (write them in the CSV): **R11/R12 first and to 0.1% --
they ARE the noise source, 4kTR is the drive, and their measured value is an input to
the 4kT gate.** Then R1-R4, R7-R10 and R13-R16 (2-wire), and the lab temperature AT
R11/R12 (not the wall): 4kT moves 0.34%/degC. Compute the gain from the measured
R7/R9/R13/R15 rather than nominal -- gain enters the 4kT slope SQUARED. Also
C1, C2 on the DMM's capacitance range, and MATCH them: `Sigma = c G^-1` needs c1 = c2,
so pick the closest pair out of the bag. The analysis uses these readings throughout --
the noise spectra cannot give C independently.

## Bring-up order

1. **Wire power off.** Series-track the PSU to +/-12 V. Verify +12 at PWR_P, -12 at
   col 51 and 0 V at GND with the DMM before enabling.
   FIRST POWER-ON AT 10-15 mA, not 50: a 180-degree-rotated adapter swaps V+ and V-,
   and a 50 mA limit will not save the part. Raise to 50 mA after the DC check passes.
2. **DC operating point** -- 60 seconds with the DMM, catches almost every build error:
   stage-1 out (j46 ch A / h54 ch B -- NOT j54, that hole carries the
   stage1-OUT -> stage2-IN+ wire; g54 is free too) = 0 +/- 5 mV;
   stage-2 out (b47 / b55) = 0 +/- 100 mV;
   nodes ~= 0.68x stage-2 out. Anything railed at +/-11 V: stop. Then 200 ns/div on
   each stage output and look for oscillation.
3. **Amplifier screen (source shorted):** `spectra.py screen` -- expect ~6.5 nV/rtHz
   FLAT (5.2 from the OPA2189 plus 3.86 from the R7||R9 feedback network). An f^-2
   skirt or two-level switching is popcorn: reject that sample.
4. **4kT gate:** `spectra.py fit4kt` over R = 1k/10k/47k/100k. The linear coefficient
   must be 4kT. **Nothing proceeds until this passes.** There is no level trim:
   levels follow from 4kTR and the fixed gain (predict: node1 2.42 mV / node2 1.99 mV
   with R3 out; 1.99 / 1.76 mV coupled).

## Configurations

- **Coupled (the experiment):** as listed.
- **Node 1 alone (calibration):** pull R3 out. Node 1 = R1, C1 only.
- **Node 2 alone (calibration):** pull R3 out. Node 2 = R2, C2, R4.
- **Source independence check (the go/no-go):** both sources live -> scope N_OUT1 vs
  N_OUT2, expect rho ~= 0. To kill a source, **SHORT R11/R12** -- never lift it.
  Shorting lowers the input impedance so it cannot leave a floating node or start an
  oscillation; lifting does both, and that wrecked three separate tests on 2026-09-08.
  Two separate resistors are independent by construction, so a non-zero rho here is
  coupling in the board or the measurement, not the sources.
- Spare holes a30 and b32 are on node 2 if a third lead is ever needed.
